original.title: An Ice-Covered Ocean on Snowball Earth — Where Might Life Hide? 🧊
original.banner: Earth freezes over. Where does life hide?
original.hook_vo: An ocean sealed by ice. Where could life survive?
original.art_direction: Glacial cyan and white under a pale dim sun, crystalline ice textures, macro-to-wide contrast, black abyss below.

options.label: Inside a frozen wave
options.image_prompt: A towering breaking wave frozen solid on a white Cryogenian sea, crystal-blue ice curling overhead, pale dim sun behind, photoreal painterly, vertical composition, one warm focal light from the low sun

options.label: Frozen shoreline boulders
options.image_prompt: Ice-glazed boulders on a frozen shoreline of bare rock, no plants anywhere, white sea ice to the horizon, photoreal painterly, vertical composition, one warm focal light from a pale sunset

options.label: Snowfield at the equator
options.vo: On the equator's frozen snow field.
options.image_prompt: An empty level Cryogenian snowfield seen close above its unbroken surface. Shallow wind-carved sastrugi form fine parallel white ridges across the foreground and continue onto a broad flat snowy plain. Fine granular snow crystals are readable on the near ridges. A very narrow strip of pale cyan sky lies at the upper edge, a tiny cold sun diffused through haze. A restrained warm reflection grazes one snow ridge. The entire ground is continuous snow with no exposed dark gap. Only snow, ice and sky.
options.art_direction: Close granular white sastrugi on a continuous flat snowfield, a narrow pale cyan sky and restrained warm reflected sunlight.

options.label: Deep hydrothermal vent
options.vo: Sink to a deep hydrothermal vent.
options.image_prompt: A deep-ocean hydrothermal vent chimney in dark liquid water, dark mineral-rich fluid rising into cold seawater, pale microbial mats visible on the surrounding rock, no boiling bubbles, no molten rock, no glowing chimney, photoreal painterly, vertical composition, one warm focal light from soft amber cinematic fill on the nearby pale minerals

options.label: Drifting ice floe
options.vo: A slab of drifting sea ice.
options.image_prompt: An isolated small flat sea-ice floe drifting in a broad pool of slushy grey-green seawater. An elevated oblique documentary composition shows the entire irregular pale blue slab and all of its edges, surrounded on every side by water and tiny loose ice fragments. Subtle shallow waves and frothy slush touch its thin vertical sides. The slab occupies the middle half of the frame, with green-grey water in every corner. A restrained warm sunset reflection lies on the water at the upper right. Empty Cryogenian ocean detail, only one separate slab and natural slush.
options.art_direction: Elevated view of one fully separate pale blue ice slab surrounded by grey-green slushy seawater, warm reflected sunset at the upper right.

options.label: Glacier crevasse
options.image_prompt: natural-history documentary view looking down into a deep blue glacier crevasse, walls of layered ice vanishing into darkness, photoreal painterly, vertical composition, one warm focal light from faint sunlight from above

options.label: Frozen salt flat
options.image_prompt: Close downward natural-history view of an ancient frozen salt pan. Opaque chalk-white mineral crust forms small irregular polygon cells with thin dark hairline seams. Tiny granular salt crystals and a light dusting of frost cover the near polygon rims. Dry opaque cream and pale pink mineral crust fills the entire frame from edge to edge. A low restrained amber sidelight reveals the granular surface. The ground is a level continuous mineral pan; there is no deep opening or visible sea.
options.art_direction: Downward macro detail of opaque white and pale pink salt polygons, granular frost and thin hairline seams under restrained amber sidelight.

options.label: Top of the ice sheet
options.vo: Climb to the top of the ice sheet.
options.image_prompt: The uppermost broad rounded snow dome of a thick Cryogenian ice sheet at blue hour, seen from a distant elevated natural-history viewpoint. Soft wind-streaked snow covers the entire gently convex summit; shallow sculpted ridges cross the near slope and airborne spindrift skims its surface. The smooth ice dome fills the lower two thirds of the frame and curves gently toward a small band of starry deep blue sky. A thin restrained amber dawn rim touches its far upper edge. The landscape is completely unoccupied, only natural snow and sky.
options.art_direction: A broad empty convex ice-sheet summit, shallow blue wind-sculpted snow, spindrift and starry deep blue sky with a thin amber dawn rim.

original.verdict_vo: Real answer: number 4, because scientists propose life used chemicals near deep sea vents to survive. A possible refuge beneath the ice.

fact.text: One proposed refuge for life during Snowball Earth was deep-ocean hydrothermal vents powered by chemicals rather than sunlight.
fact.source_sentence: In reservoirs of anaerobic and low-oxygen life powered by chemicals in deep oceanic hydrothermal vents surviving in Earth's deep oceans and crust; but photosynthesis would not have been possible there.

original.description: Hundreds of millions of years ago, ice may have reached the equator. Eight places for life to wait out Snowball Earth, and the one scientists keep coming back to.
original.related_topic_hint: Snowball Earth: The Planet That Froze
